title: Best 3D Product Animators (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a 3D product animator: what the package should include, what to send, what drives the price and the red flags to avoid.
intro: 3D product animation shows a product from every angle, explodes it into parts, or demonstrates features that are hard to film. It is common for gadgets, cosmetics, furniture and products that do not exist yet. Projects go wrong when the model is inaccurate, the materials look fake, or the product details are not final when modeling starts. This guide helps you get an animation that looks real and stays accurate.

faq.q: Do I need a 3D model already?
faq.a: Not always. If you have CAD files or 3D models from manufacturing, send them. Otherwise the animator builds a model from photos, drawings and measurements, which takes more time.
It depends on the model, materials, lighting and rendering time. Ask for samples of similar products, such as glass, metal or fabric, since some materials are harder to make realistic.

faq.q: Can I also get still images?
faq.a: Often yes. Once the model exists, still renders for your store or ads are relatively quick. Ask to include them.
Usually MP4 videos in the sizes you need, plus still images. Ask whether the 3D model and project files are included.
Agree in writing. Owning the model lets you reuse it for future videos and images.
